\section{The literal feedback map and theorem ceiling}

For $n\geq1$, put $\X_n=[n]^{[n]}$ and regard
$f\in\X_n$ both as an endofunction and as the word
$f(0)\cdots f(n-1)$.  Define the self-map $\M_n:\X_n\to\X_n$ by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:literal}
 (\M_n f)(i)=
 \begin{cases}
   \min\{j\in[n]:f(j)=i\},&f^{-1}(i)\ne\varnothing,\\
   i,&f^{-1}(i)=\varnothing.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
The second line is part of the map, not an arbitrary completion of a
partial section.  Powers $\M_n^k$ below mean repeated feedback under
\eqref{eq:literal}, not composition powers of the original $f$.

The first line chooses the least member of each kernel class.  Least kernel
transversals and inverse matchings in transformation semigroups are
established background \cite{FernandesEtAl2009,Higgins2019}.  Indeed,
$f\circ\M_n(f)\circ f=f$, and
$e_f=\M_n(f)\circ f$ is the idempotent retraction sending each position to
the least member of its $\ker f$ block.  This does not make $\M_n$ a mutual
inverse selection: for $f=(0,0)$, $\M_2(f)=\id$ but
$\M_2(f)\circ f\circ\M_2(f)=f\ne\M_2(f)$.  The identity-on-missing rule is
what controls subsequent path splitting.

First-occurrence encodings and their set-partition interpretation are also
classical \cite{BeanEtAl2026}, as are functional-digraph decomposition
\cite{FlajoletOdlyzko1989} and periodic-point zeta functions
\cite{ArtinMazur1965}.  These ingredients, involution and Bell numbers,
and labelled-set calculus receive no contribution credit.  The result
proved here is only the exact conjunction forced by the literal rule
\eqref{eq:literal}.  No novelty or priority conclusion is drawn from the
bounded owner search.

For $x\in\X_n$, let $\tail(x)$ be its least entrance time into the recurrent
set and let $\per(x)$ be its eventual period.  Write
$\Y_n=\M_n(\X_n)$, let $R_n$ be the number of recurrent points, and let
$I_n$ be the number of involutions of $[n]$.  Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:involution-egf}
 \sum_{n\geq0}I_n\frac{x^n}{n!}=\exp(x+x^2/2).
\end{equation}

We also prepare the target-local inverse notation.  Given $g\in\X_n$, put
\[
 U_g=\{i:g(i)\ne i\}.
\]
If the values $\{g(i):i\in U_g\}$ repeat, define $\Phi_n(g)=0$.  Otherwise
set
\[
 F_g=\{i:g(i)=i,\ i\notin g(U_g)\}.
\]
For $A\subseteq F_g$, let $P_A=U_g\cup A$ and
\[
 r_A(i)=\begin{cases}g(i),&i\in U_g,\\i,&i\in A,\end{cases}
 \qquad R_A=\{r_A(i):i\in P_A\},
\]
and define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:phi}
 \Phi_n(g)=\sum_{A\subseteq F_g}
 \prod_{\substack{0\leq j<n\\j\notin R_A}}
 \bigl|\{i\in P_A:r_A(i)<j\}\bigr|.
\end{equation}
Empty products have value one; a zero factor rejects that choice of $A$.

\begin{theorem}[complete dynamics and one-step fibres]\label{thm:main}
For the literal map \eqref{eq:literal}, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item Every component of every $g\in\Y_n$ is either a directed cycle or a
loop-rooted directed path.  One update inverts each cycle.  If a path of
size $s>1$ in root-to-leaf order is $P=(p_0,\ldots,p_{s-1})$, one update
reverses $P$ when $p_0>p_1$, and otherwise splits off $p_0$ and reverses the
remaining path; a singleton is fixed.
For $n\geq2$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:heights}
 \max_{f\in\X_n}\tail(f)=2n-2,
 \qquad \max_{g\in\Y_n}\tail(g)=2n-3.
\end{equation}
Both maxima are zero at $n=1$.

\item A path of size $s>1$ is recurrent exactly when
$p_0>p_1$ and $p_{s-1}>p_{s-2}$; a singleton is fixed.  On a prescribed
$s$-set, the number $c_s$ of connected recurrent states is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:connected}
 c_1=1,\quad c_2=1,\quad c_3=4,\qquad
 c_s=(s-1)!+\frac{s!}{4}\quad(s\geq4).
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rec-egf}
 \sum_{n\geq0}R_n\frac{x^n}{n!}
 =\frac{1}{1-x}\exp\!\left(\frac{x^3}{3}
       +\frac{x^4}{4(1-x)}\right).
\end{equation}

\item The fixed states are precisely the involutions.  For every $k\geq1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-fix}
 |\Fix(\M_n^k)|=
 \begin{cases}I_n,&k\text{ odd},\\R_n,&k\text{ even}.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
The finite-map dynamical zeta function, as a formal power series, is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:zeta}
 \zeta_{\M_n}(z)=(1-z)^{-I_n}
 (1-z^2)^{-(R_n-I_n)/2}.
\end{equation}

\item For every target $g\in\X_n$, including targets outside $\Y_n$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibre}
 |\M_n^{-1}(g)|=\Phi_n(g).
\end{equation}
If $B_n$ is the $n$th Bell number, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bell}
 \max_{g\in\X_n}|\M_n^{-1}(g)|=B_n,
\end{equation}
and the identity target attains the maximum.

\item The first three nonempty carriers have the following boundary data;
``two-orbits'' counts dynamical orbits rather than points.

```text
1, 2, 5, 9, 15, 30, 45.
```

The proof also classifies every fixed point and strict two-cycle and gives
ordinary generating functions for both classes.  The independent inverse
side remains the every-target one-step fibre coefficient in Section 4.2.
Thus the former proof hold is closed.  `CT1` receives
`PROMOTE_INTERNAL_THEOREM_READY_OWNER_HOLD`: the mathematics is coherent
enough for internal development, while priority, specialist ownership, and
external release remain unresolved.

\section{The operation and its scope}

Let $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and $\X_n=[n]^{[n]}$, with $n\ge0$.
For each nonempty fibre $f^{-1}(v)=\{i_1<\cdots<i_k\}$, set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rule}
 (Tf)(i_j)=i_{j+1}\quad(1\le j<k),
 \qquad (Tf)(i_k)=v.
\end{equation}
Every fibre and its order are computed from the old function. Since the
fibres partition $[n]$, this simultaneous prescription defines
$T:\X_n\to\X_n$. The empty function is fixed. We retain all labels;
there is no quotient by rotation or graph isomorphism.

The functional digraph of $f$ has arrows $i\to f(i)$. Its directed
cycles, including loops, are called \emph{vertex cycles}. In contrast,
$f$ is \emph{recurrent} when $T^p(f)=f$ for some $p\ge1$, and
$\per(f)$ is the least such $p$. These refer to the update on whole
functions. Every permutation is fixed by \eqref{eq:rule}, whatever its
vertex-cycle lengths, but nonpermutations can have nontrivial periods:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-cycle}
 (1,2,1)\ \longmapsto\ (2,2,1)\ \longmapsto\ (1,2,1).
\end{equation}
Here $1\leftrightarrow2$ is unchanged and the arrow from vertex $0$
alternates between its two attachments.

Our results answer two separate questions. Section~\ref{sec:recurrence}
classifies exactly the labelled graphs supporting recurrent motion and
determines their periods. Section~\ref{sec:inverse} reconstructs every
one-step predecessor directly from the target and proves that the cyclic
successor permutation uniquely maximizes the fibre, with value $2^{n-1}$
for $n\ge1$. All proofs are given here; finite checks are supplementary.

\paragraph{Known rewiring primitives.}
Replacing ordered stars by chains is established graph linearization.
Onus, Richa and Scheideler's pure linearization algorithm operates on
connected undirected graphs, separates smaller and larger neighbours, and
uses an add-wins convention when updates conflict
\citep[Algorithm~1 and Section~2]{onus2007linearization}.
Connectivity by replacing old edges with paths is also a shared primitive.
Those operations and their proofs are not claimed as new here.

The successor-repair protocols of Cramer and Fuhrmann
\citep[Sections~4 and 5.1--5.3]{cramer2005ring} and Shaker and Reeves
\citep[Figure~3 and Section~5.1]{shaker2005ring} provide a closer directed
comparison. Their successor changes shorten clockwise successor distance.
In \eqref{eq:two-cycle}, the successor of $0$ instead moves from $1$ to
$2$ before returning. Thus this loop-free transition is neither a literal
successor repair nor a batch consisting only of such shortening repairs.
This witness does not exclude every abstract conjugacy or enlarged-state
construction. Aradhya and Scheideler's tree-to-path construction
\citep[Section~3.4, Algorithm~10 and Appendix~B]{aradhya2025tree}
also rewires ordered siblings, but takes a rooted tree with depth-parity
labels; its distributed version additionally has supervisor and message
state. It is not repeated \eqref{eq:rule} on arbitrary endofunctions with
vertex cycles. We credit these primitives, ordinary path covers and
rotation/LCM calculations. The contribution here is the exact recurrent
and inverse/extremal conjunction for \eqref{eq:rule}, not a general
rewiring method or a global priority claim.

## SI mathematics and decisive subtraction

Complete proofs: `SI_PROOF_AND_ADAPTER.md`.
The full height is n-1; first-image height max(n-2,0); the recurrent
set is S_n with inversion dynamics. For n>=3 there are 2n! deepest states.
Every first image is cycles plus loop-rooted paths. SI always splits off
the current root and reverses the rest of each path.

For any target with distinct nonfixed coordinate values, let k be its
number of fixed vertices and p its number of nontrivial path components.
Its fibre is

    N(k,p)=sum_{s=0}^{k-p} binom(k-p,s)
             sum_b {k-s brace b}_{>=2} (k-s)_b.

This counts forced unique occurrences followed by free assignments to
fixed labels, with singleton fibres allowed only at their own label.
Targets with repeated nonfixed values have zero fibre; among remaining
targets only (k,p)=(1,1) is unsupported. Identity uniquely maximizes,
with fibres 1,3,10,65,456 for n=1..5. An independent algebraic expression
within the **author-side** pilot uses rook inclusion-exclusion; the
second checker instead uses no-singleton partitions and compares all
decoded predecessor sets, not only counts.

P167 owns the same first-image component lemma and already contains the
split-root/reverse-rest branch; SI merely makes that branch unconditional.
The temporal proof therefore transfers. Conversely, SI is not a literal
P167 iterate: g=(2,0,2) is P167-periodic, whereas SI erodes it to identity.
SI's n=3 identity fibre10 also exceeds P167's Bell ceiling5, blocking
transfer of its kernel-partition injection. These differences establish

## 4. `CT1`: all-weight theorem package and owner gate

### 4.1 Literal group reduction

Let `sigma` have `m_j` cycles of length `j`.  The classical centralizer
decomposition gives

```text
C_(S_n)(sigma) = product_j W_(j,m_j),
W_(j,m) = C_j^m semidirect S_m.
